papers.title: Making MLLM Latents Matter: Factor-Aware Predictive Learning for Cinematic Video Generation

summary.tldr: Factor-Aware Predictive Learning (FAPL) uses a multi-stage framework to optimize Multimodal LLM latents for Video Diffusion Transformers, enabling improved factor-aware control and temporal inference in cinematic video generation.
key_points: Latent-only generator grounding trains the DiT with a frozen MLLM and connector to force reliance on MLLM representations.
Factor-span replacement uses paired video data to enforce target-factor modification while keeping non-target factors preserved.
Temporal inference training optimizes the MLLM and connector through a frozen DiT using text-only and complete-observation video targets.
summary.why_it_matters: It bridges MLLM representations with video diffusion backbones to enhance control over sparse-to-video, editing, and multi-shot cinematic generation tasks.

papers.title: Deep Search in Real-World Web Environments

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced OpenDS, a task for evaluating multi-step deep search agents on the live Web, along with OpenDS-World, a benchmark of 200 human-verified tasks spanning diverse modalities and interactive requirements.
key_points: OpenDS-World evaluates autonomous agents across 200 tasks featuring heterogeneous file formats, multiple modalities, and interactive access controls on the live open Web.
Evaluating 12 frontier models in a unified tool environment showed the top-performing agent reached 39.0% accuracy.
Human baseline testing across 1,000 independent attempts achieved a 21.1% accuracy rate.
Analysis highlighted key performance bottlenecks in tool coordination, search cost, termination behavior, and long-horizon search management.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a realistic, live-Web benchmark for measuring and improving how autonomous agents navigate complex interactive environments to gather multi-source evidence.

papers.title: WeVisOne-VL: Unified Visual Perception from Objects to Pixels

summary.tldr: WeVisOne-VL unifies object-level and pixel-level visual perception within a single vision-language model using structured next-token prediction and an integrated lightweight pixel decoder.
key_points: Integrates a lightweight pixel decoder into the VLM via a special token to support output formats ranging from points and bounding boxes to masks and alpha mattes.
Unifies diverse perception tasks including object detection, referring localization, counting, OCR, segmentation, and matting.
Trained using a three-stage curriculum Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) strategy followed by mixed-task Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Maintains robust rejection mechanisms for queries regarding absent objects while achieving top performance across more than 30 benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: By unifying granular object and pixel-level tasks into one open-source VLM, it advances vision-language models toward reliable real-world deployment across multi-granularity localization tasks.

papers.title: Editing Images into Reusable Layers via Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation

summary.tldr: LayerEditor unifies instruction-guided image editing and layer decomposition by using In-Context RGB-Alpha Token Modeling and Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation to generate reusable, editable RGBA layers.
key_points: In-Context RGB-Alpha Token Modeling jointly formats the edited canvas and an ordered sequence of RGBA layers into a single token sequence.
Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation transfers the pretrained model's edit prior to both the target canvas and the composite of predicted layers to prevent capability loss.
Introduces LayerEditor-100K, a large-scale dataset containing paired image-editing instruction data and ordered RGBA layer annotations.
Supports dual capabilities of instruction-based editing and explicit layer-level decomposition for flexible downstream manipulation.
summary.why_it_matters: By decoupling flat image edits into ordered RGBA layers, it enables precise non-destructive local editing and reuse of individual elements in graphic workflows.

papers.title: IQuest-Q1: Advancing Foundation Capabilities for Agentic CLI Systems

summary.tldr: IQuest-Q1 is an open-source 320B sparse MoE agentic foundation model (15B activated) trained via a three-stage pipeline and expert model merging for CLI systems.
key_points: Architecture features 320 billion total parameters with 15 billion parameters activated per forward pass.
Pre-training uses Stable SplitNorm, Muon, muP, and a two-stage curriculum that increases coding data in the second stage.
Mid-training extends context length and broadens data mixtures across domains and formats.
Post-training combines SFT, domain-specialized RL, and Multi-Objective Policy Optimization (MOPD) across diverse scaffolds.
Model merging combines experts and checkpoints across stages while resolving parameter update conflicts.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers an open-source, highly parameter-efficient MoE foundation model specialized for agentic coding and general-purpose CLI capabilities.

papers.title: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI

summary.tldr: A new review frames recursive self-improvement for robot learning, mapping how physical agents can advance from improving task performance to improving their underlying learning processes.
key_points: Digital self-improvement relies on code rewriting and executable tests, whereas physical RSI must manage partial observations, costly real-world trials, non-stationary conditions, and irreversible actions.
Self-improvement gains persist only if feedback addresses learning needs, the target module can absorb changes, value survives task or hardware updates, and trials remain safe and affordable.

Current physical studies, mostly in robot manipulation, demonstrate behavioral gains and tool/knowledge updates, but none have yet isolated performance improvements specifically attributable to recursive loops.
The authors establish evaluation principles and research directions to design physical systems that safely refine their own improvement mechanisms over repeated trials.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a structured framework to evaluate whether physical robots can safely and autonomously optimize their own learning pipelines beyond simple task-level adaptation.

papers.title: Policy-Mask: Budget-Aware Adaptation of Diffusion Features to Discriminative Tasks

summary.tldr: Policy-Mask is a budget-conditioned policy that jointly selects optimal timesteps, network blocks, and channel subsets from frozen diffusion models for downstream discriminative tasks under explicit channel constraints.
key_points: Jointly optimizes timestep, block depth, and channel subset selection under a prescribed budget using a cardinality-normalized loss to stabilize multi-head updates.
Adapts across architectures by swapping U-Net channels for image-token hidden dimensions in Diffusion Transformers like PixArt-Σ and SD3.5 MMDiT.
Achieves downstream performance of 38.9 mIoU on ADE20K, 75.4% top-1 accuracy on CIFAR-100 (at 128 dimensions), and 76.3 PCK@0.1 on SPair-71k.
Identifies 256 retained channels as the optimal operating point for compact diffusion representations based on budget score ablations.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates manual feature extraction heuristics, providing an automated method to compress diffusion model representations while maximizing downstream task performance.

papers.title: Deep Fusion Memory: A Chunk-Level Parametric Memory for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: Deep Fusion Memory (DFM) is a chunk-level parametric memory architecture that predicts external memory from context and fuses it into frozen LLM intermediate hidden states via gated cross-attention without online retrieval.
key_points: Trains memory prediction and fusion end-to-end using gated cross-attention into intermediate hidden states while keeping the base LLM backbone frozen.
Uses a causal memory predictor supervised by retrieved chunk embeddings from the corpus, sharing predicted memory across tokens within each chunk.
Reduces offline training data construction workload by requiring 32x fewer retrieval queries and 2048x fewer retrieved items compared to token-level parametric memory baselines.
Outperforms top baselines on six QA tasks by 12.71% on Mistral-7B-v0.3 and 11.19% on Qwen3-8B-Base, while improving domain adaptation by up to 6.51 points.
summary.why_it_matters: DFM enables zero-retrieval-overhead knowledge integration during inference while drastically reducing the data preparation compute required for parametric memory training.

papers.title: LaLa-World: Scaling Latent World Models with Natural Language Actions

summary.tldr: LaLa-World introduces a language-conditioned JEPA-style latent world model that standardizes heterogeneous action formats into natural language, enabling cross-domain pretraining with 13.9x faster MPC planning than video generation baselines.
key_points: Unifies numerical actions and visual changes into natural language descriptions, allowing a single future predictor to train across simulation, robot trajectories, and web video data.
Implements the future predictor using a language model backbone to process language conditions while predicting future latent states.
Achieves 13.9x faster planning speed and 6x lower training costs compared to an RAEv2-based video generation model baseline while maintaining comparable planning performance.
Serves as a pretrained backbone for LaLa-Policy (joint action and latent visual prediction), matching Cosmos Policy performance on LIBERO and RoboCasa with up to 5.5x faster inference.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that latent world models can scale efficiently across diverse robotic and video datasets using language interfaces, significantly lowering the computational overhead of simulation-based planning and policy execution.

papers.title: Meta Expert: Cross-Layer Expert Sharing for Storage- and Retrieval-Efficient MoE

summary.tldr: Meta Expert introduces cross-layer expert sharing in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures to eliminate inter-layer redundancy and create flexible residual pathways for hidden states.
key_points: Replaces layer-specific Local Experts with cross-layer Meta Experts to address content similarity and redundancy across hierarchical MoE layers.
Matches Vanilla MoE performance using only 70% to 80% of total experts while keeping activated expert counts and granularity fixed.
Demonstrates lower cross-entropy loss, higher downstream task accuracy, and reduced parameter redundancy in multi-dimensional empirical tests.
Theoretical analysis confirms Meta Experts improve information retrieval efficiency by providing hidden states with more flexible residual pathways.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces MoE parameter redundancy and memory storage requirements while improving information storage and retrieval efficiency without sacrificing model accuracy.

papers.title: Code2Video-Compass: A Comprehensive Benchmark for General-Purpose Code-Based Video Generation across T2V, I2V, and V2V

summary.tldr: Code2Video-Compass is a general-purpose benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal LLMs on code-based video generation across text-to-video, image-to-video, and video-to-video tasks.
key_points: Comprises 2,104 tasks spanning 10 categories, 24 subtypes, and three complexity dimensions: construction, dynamic animation, and state dependency.
Supports Text-to-Video (T2V), Image-to-Video (I2V), and Video-to-Video (V2V) generation settings using curated textual instructions and visual references.

Employs a dual-level evaluation framework combining 12 objective metrics (measuring operational performance, video quality, text-video alignment, and reference fidelity) and five subjective metrics via an MLLM judge.
Benchmarked 15 proprietary and open-weight MLLMs from nine families, revealing that model performance declines as task complexity increases.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a standardized framework to measure and advance the ability of multimodal LLMs to translate complex visual and temporal requirements into executable video generation code.

papers.title: Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents

summary.tldr: Heartbeat Thinking enables voice agents to speculatively execute reasoning and tools during user speech without canceling ongoing invocations when input transcripts update.
key_points: Periodic Thinker invocations query the latest partial transcript alongside a shared state of prior completed reasoning and tool outputs.
Unlike chunk-bounded or interrupt-on-update baselines, ongoing invocations and dispatched tool calls run to completion across speech updates.
Preserving ongoing computation resolves missing tool arguments incrementally and allows execution of dependent tool chains.
Evaluated on SpeechFCEval, FDBench v3, and AudioCRAG, outperforming windowed baselines like SHANKS.
Achieves a 16 percentage point increase in speculative tool coverage and a 36.4% reduction in mean final-response latency on FDBench v3.
summary.why_it_matters: It decouples speculative computation from speech-chunk updates, converting user speaking time into execution time to significantly reduce voice agent response latency.

papers.title: Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation

summary.tldr: Cola2 introduces a co-adaptive hierarchical language modeling framework using dynamic semantic span segmentation, continuous-discrete co-adaptation, and block-causal masked diffusion decoding.
key_points: Uses auxiliary-loss-free negative feedback to control the semantic span compression rate and combines reconstruction with generation supervision.
Decouples Flow Matching prior learning from representation learning via a stop-gradient, while updating the encoder through token-prediction gradients.
Employs a block-causal masked diffusion decoder trained with clean, noisy, and dropped latent conditions, applying classifier-free guidance at inference.
Re-encodes generated text under a fixed span layout during inference to maintain latent history consistency.
Achieves a 60.10 average score across eight tasks using 346.03 billion tokens, outperforming Llama-3-8B on HellaSwag and StoryCloze.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that continuous-latent hierarchical language models can achieve highly competitive, unsaturated scaling performance compared to standard autoregressive models using significantly fewer training tokens.

papers.title: Beyond Watching and Searching: Benchmarking Agents for Video-centered Deep Research Reports

summary.tldr: Researchers introduce Video-Centered Deep Research Report Generation and OmniDR-Bench to evaluate agents synthesizing external multimodal evidence into interactive, video-grounded reports.
key_points: OmniDR-Bench comprises 50 bilingual (Chinese and English) tasks across 19 subcategories with 6,414 atomic criteria.

Introduces Omni Atomic Rubric Trees (Omni-ARTs), evaluating tasks across three dimensions, 23 shared directions, and atomic binary criteria for audiovisual grounding, multimodal evidence, and interactivity.
Employs Audited Rubric Construction (ARC) combining independent evidence collection, automated checks, behavioral calibration, and iterative human review.
Evaluating 18 agent configurations revealed a top score of 63.3 out of 100, highlighting deficiencies in causal analysis, content coverage, and citation accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on their ability to cross-reference video content with web evidence to produce verifiable, interactive deep research reports.

papers.title: RouteWeaver: Weaving Mode Selection and Execution into Unified LLM Routing

summary.tldr: RouteWeaver is a unified LLM routing framework that dynamically learns both mode selection and model execution within a single policy using COMET-GRPO and progressive exploration.
key_points: Unifies single-round, multi-round, and agentic routing modes into a single LLM router policy.
Uses COMET-GRPO (COordinated Mode-Execution Training) to decouple trajectory-level advantages into distinct credit assignment signals for mode selection and within-mode execution.
Applies progressive exploration to transition training from externally assigned modes to autonomous selection, preventing policy collapse to single-round execution.
Achieved an average accuracy of 61.4% across five domains (math, coding, knowledge, logic, facts), representing an 11.03% relative improvement over the strongest baseline.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables LLM routers to flexibly adapt their execution paradigm to query complexity rather than relying on fixed, predefined interaction structures.

papers.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning

summary.tldr: A new thought pruning method optimizes pass@k directly over candidate solution pools during test-time scaling, automatically balancing solution quality and diversity.
key_points: Test-time scaling prunes candidate reasoning trajectories after a short prefix to reduce computation, but existing methods optimize quality or diversity in isolation.
The proposed method maximizes the probability that at least one selected partial solution yields a correct answer when completed.
The pass@k objective naturally incorporates quality while penalizing trajectory redundancy, avoiding ad-hoc trade-off mechanisms.
Evaluated across eight open-weight reasoning models, outperforming prior quality-based and diversity-based pruning strategies, particularly when retaining a moderate number of partial solutions.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly optimizing pass@k reduces the computational cost of test-time scaling without sacrificing inference accuracy or candidate diversity.

papers.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models

summary.tldr: Quantizing language model n-gram embedding tables to 4-bit precision reduces table memory requirements by up to 75% while retaining over 99% of their validation loss gains.
key_points: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash allocates 196 billion parameters strictly to its Engram n-gram memory.
Four-bit quantization saves ~75% memory on models trained from scratch (nanochat, Llama, and GPT-2 families) while preserving >99% of validation-loss improvements.
Post-training quantization on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next cuts table memory by 47-55% with <1.2% perplexity increase and minimal downstream impact.
Performance drops at sub-4-bit precisions can be largely recovered using a short fine-tuning phase.
Memory savings can be reinvested into larger n-gram tables to outperform full-precision baselines while maintaining a lower total memory footprint.
summary.why_it_matters: Low-bit quantization significantly lowers the massive memory footprint of n-gram embedding tables in modern language models without sacrificing model accuracy or downstream performance.

papers.title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation

summary.tldr: CausalCoT mitigates attention leakage by structuring step-by-step reasoning into a directed acyclic graph and evaluating each atomic sub-question within an isolated context containing only its direct causal parents.
key_points: Decomposes complex problems into a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of atomic sub-questions to enforce a Markovian dependency structure.
Eliminates direct attention pathways to non-parent context, preventing models from relying on global lookup while generating post-hoc rationales.
Increases the causal sensitivity of intermediate reasoning steps by an average of 12 and up to 21 percentage points over the strongest baseline.
Enables test-time interventions where local step corrections predictably propagate through downstream nodes in the graph.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves the faithfulness of model rationales and allows predictable, localized test-time interventions without degrading baseline predictive performance.

papers.title: What Makes a Good Unmasking Policy? A Controlled Study of Learned Unmasking in Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: A 856K-parameter learned unmasking policy trained on trajectory-contraction targets achieves an optimal accuracy-speed frontier for masked diffusion language models by combining confidence scores with hidden states.
key_points: Labeling predictions that match the final output as committable is overly permissive at low numbers of function evaluations (NFE).
Hidden states perform weakly as policy inputs on their own, but effectively complement confidence scores.
A 10% reduction in NFE offsets the computational overhead for unmasking policies up to 7.5 million parameters.
The 856K-parameter policy trained on LLaDA-8B-Instruct achieves top throughput and accuracy frontiers on GSM8K and transfers to Dream-7B-Instruct.
summary.why_it_matters: Learned unmasking policies can significantly boost diffusion language model throughput with minimal overhead, provided they are trained on trajectory-contraction targets using both confidence and hidden state inputs.

papers.title: When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation (AOPD) improves online policy distillation by weighting teacher actions based on their counterfactual advantage under the student, using only standard student rollouts.
key_points: Identifies that conventional Online Policy Distillation (OPD) uniformly enforces teacher guidance without evaluating whether specific teacher actions improve student performance.
Introduces AOPD, which weights teacher actions by their counterfactual advantage under the student policy to reinforce beneficial actions and downweight unhelpful ones.
Derives an estimator that computes advantage-weighted supervision using teacher importance weights on student-sampled actions, requiring zero extra rollouts or reward evaluations.
Demonstrates performance improvements over standard distillation and RL baselines across math, coding, and MedQA tasks in both self-distillation and external-teacher setups.
summary.why_it_matters: AOPD increases distillation efficiency and model accuracy by filtering out unhelpful teacher guidance without incurring the extra compute cost of counterfactual rollouts.

papers.title: Beyond Causal Masks: Auditing and Localizing Hidden Future-Token Leakage in Adaptive Sequence Models

summary.tldr: Researchers identified and repaired hidden future-token leakage in an adaptive sequence model, where a full-sequence routing summary violated causal invariance despite a correct causal attention mask.
key_points: An anomalous 24-layer adaptive residual-routing checkpoint reduced teacher-forced validation loss from 3.5958 to 1.4259, but failed prefix-invariance audits and degraded during free-running generation.
Layer-wise diagnostics traced the causal breach to a full-sequence routing summary broadcast through the model's dynamic routing-query path.
Audits were executed using prefix-invariance contracts, maximum prefix-output discrepancy (LeakScore), behavioral metrics, and numerical precision cache-consistency checks.
Two 12-layer causal repairs successfully eliminated the leakage, restoring validation loss and reference perplexity to expected baseline control scales.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrating that lower teacher-forced loss can stem from structural information leaks highlights the need to pair standard evaluations with free-running generation and explicit causal audits.

papers.title: How Depth Growth and Looping Shape In-Context Learning in Language Models

summary.tldr: Depth-grown and looped language models exhibit a shared inductive bias that accelerates the acquisition, strengthens the retention, and alters the underlying attention mechanisms of in-context learning compared to dense reference models.
key_points: Evaluated parameter reuse across pretrained language models up to 3B parameters and controlled tasks.
Depth-grown and looped models acquire in-context learning (ICL) earlier in training and retain it better when competing against weight-based associations.
Tracing attention heads shows that depth growth actively propagates early induction heads into deeper layers.
Ablation studies demonstrate a stronger reliance on induction-ranked heads for both few-shot performance and later-token prediction in parameter-reused architectures.
summary.why_it_matters: Architectures utilizing soft parameter reuse or depth growth inherently bias language models toward dynamic in-context reasoning over static weight memorization.

papers.title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression

summary.tldr: TTR-Compressor introduces a sequence compression method that frame input tokens as an end-to-end learned test-time regression problem with closed-form coefficient solutions.
key_points: Replaces conventional pooling and projection-based sequence compression with an end-to-end learned test-time regression formulation.
Calculates regression coefficients efficiently in closed form during the forward pass while training the underlying regression problem via backpropagation.
Outperforms standard attention-based compressors on the RULER benchmark when evaluated within block-wise sparse attention architectures.
Matches standard MLP visual token merger performance in multimodal LLMs while utilizing 55.6% fewer visual tokens.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a more parameter- and token-efficient sequence compression primitive for long-context language models and multimodal vision-language architectures.

papers.title: Diffusion Language Models for Perplexity-Aware Black-Box Attacks

summary.tldr: A continuous diffusion language model replaces the unnatural random mappings in continuous-space black-box LLM attacks, preserving Gaussian latent optimization while generating natural prompts.
key_points: Replaces random continuous-to-text mappings with a continuous diffusion language model (dLLM) tied to a standard-Gaussian latent space.
Maintains standard sampling (RareTrap) and optimization (ThinkTrap) search procedures for triggering malicious target behaviors like overthinking.
Reduces character-level perplexity from 10^3–10^7 to 3–5 in RareTrap sampling and from 20–28 to 4.3–5.4 in ThinkTrap optimization.
Demonstrates that black-box model risk estimates shift by up to an order of magnitude when using learned, natural language mappings instead of random mappings.
summary.why_it_matters: Using learned diffusion language models enables more realistic safety risk evaluations and creates adversarial attacks capable of bypassing perplexity-based input guardrails.

papers.title: Drift Says When, Budget Says How Much: Rate-Controlled KV Re-selection for Long-Form Multimodal Generation

summary.tldr: Rate-Controlled Refresh (RCR) dynamically re-selects multimodal visual KV cache tokens based on attention drift while controlling refresh frequency per sample, addressing limitations of one-shot and fixed-threshold compression methods.
key_points: One-shot prefill visual token selection achieves only 0.44-0.52 ROUGE-L agreement with uncompressed outputs on long-form generation because visual evidence needs evolve over time.

RCR uses a GPU-resident low-rank drift detector and candidate-restricted re-selection to determine when and where to re-select, using a per-sample controller to adjust refresh rates across non-comparable drift magnitudes.
Drift-driven timing in RCR outperforms random timing at the same refresh rate and periodic timing at a higher rate by 2.0-5.0 ROUGE-L points on DetailCaps.
RCR beats InfiniGen by 1.6-3.8 ROUGE-L points across five of six model-task benchmarks with a 4x smaller GPU detector footprint and performs within 1.7 points of exact per-step re-selection.
summary.why_it_matters: RCR enables accurate, long-form multimodal generation under constrained KV cache budgets by dynamically updating retained visual evidence without incurring the heavy overhead of per-step retrieval.

security.title: AgentPhishing: A Benchmark of LLM Email Agents Under Adaptive Attack

summary.tldr: AgentPhishing is a new benchmark assessing LLM email agents against adaptive, persuasive attacks optimized by a novel technique called PhishOpt.
key_points: Introduces AgentPhishing to evaluate whether LLM email agents detect persuasive phishing and comply with malicious requests.
Develops PhishOpt to optimize reusable email-generation skills against targeted agents under realism and benchmark constraints.
Categorizes attack strategies using Cialdini's persuasion principles to construct a universal attack generation skill.
Demonstrates that four out of nine tested agents had phishing-detection rates under 10% and malicious-request compliance rates over 45% despite passing conventional phishing checks.
summary.why_it_matters: Conventional phishing detection benchmarks fail to reflect agent safety, as adaptive persuasive attacks easily bypass detection and manipulate agents into executing harmful actions.

security.title: AfterDeleteBench: Auditing Post-Deletion Information Persistence in LLM Agents

summary.tldr: AfterDeleteBench introduces a controlled behavioral audit evaluating post-deletion secret persistence in LLM agents, demonstrating that deleting source memories fails to erase information stored in descendant states.
key_points: Uses matched control agents (never-exposed vs. exposed-then-deleted) to isolate post-deletion recovery caused specifically by prior exposure.
Single queries recovered deleted secrets from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in ~67% of cases, compared to 0% recovery in never-exposed controls.

Exact secret reconstruction succeeded in 62-99% of cases across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3 models when only separately stored components remained under a public composition rule, without surviving verbatim copies.
Provenance-aware closure successfully eliminated observed secret recovery, whereas exact-literal write filters blocked reinsertion but failed to erase existing persisted state.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating data deletion in LLM agents requires behavioral auditing across the entire memory and descendant state system rather than relying solely on storage-level record removal.

security.title: ReDence: A Hybrid Agentic and Decision-Model Framework for Rapid, Evidence-Grounded Detection of Modern Social Engineering Scams

summary.tldr: ReDence is an open-source hybrid framework combining a multimodal agent with a decision model to perform rapid, evidence-grounded social engineering scam detection.
key_points: Uses a dual-model system featuring a fine-tuned Qwen3.5-4B multimodal Investigator for planning and reporting, paired with a specialized Tev1 Decider for discrete binary and multiple-choice decisions.
Achieves 96% accuracy across twelve distinct social engineering scam categories by navigating website workflows and cross-referencing external evidence.
Executes detection at least four times faster than comparable pure agentic models by delegating browser actions and assessment decisions to the Tev1 model.
Generates structured, auditable reports documenting investigative actions, artifacts, and both supporting and contradictory evidence to facilitate quick takedowns.
summary.why_it_matters: The framework significantly accelerates the detection and takedown of complex online scams by automating evidence collection without sacrificing auditing depth.

security.title: Amplifying Latency and Cost of LLM Inference via Rowhammer Attack

summary.tldr: LLVMhammer uses CPU DRAM Rowhammer bit-flips in Triton's MLIR/LLVM compilation pipeline to permanently degrade GPU-based LLM inference performance without altering model code.
key_points: Target-independent Triton optimization passes are manipulated via DRAM bit-flips to generate suboptimal but functionally correct GPU kernels.
Triton's disk-caching mechanism ensures a single bit-flip causes persistent inference latency increases across subsequent executions.
The Karnage tool automatically isolates vulnerable bit-flip locations within Triton's vendor-agnostic MLIR/LLVM compilation pipeline.
Evaluated on Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, and Deepseek-7B across NVIDIA RTX 4090 and AMD RX 7900 XTX GPUs, causing 4-16% latency increases or lowering output BERTScore down to 25%.
summary.why_it_matters: The attack demonstrates that hardware-level CPU vulnerabilities can cause persistent financial and performance degradation in GPU-accelerated LLM cloud infrastructure across multiple GPU vendors.

security.title: AgentTriage: Replayable Security Diagnosis Across Heterogeneous Agent Runtimes

summary.tldr: AgentTriage is an open-source executable contract framework for deterministic, replayable security diagnosis and provenance graph construction across heterogeneous AI agent runtimes.
key_points: Uses runtime overlays to normalize heterogeneous observations into canonical events, joining invocation and result lifecycles into a typed provenance graph.
Requires deterministic claim-evidence binding and mandatory abstention when required evidence is missing, eliminating language-model judgment during diagnosis recomputation.
Evaluated across five runtimes and 120 adjudicated cases, achieving 0.858 grounded joint diagnosis, 0.966 required-evidence coverage, and a 0.036 unsupported-claim rate.
Outperformed the strongest same-schema baseline in joint diagnosis by 0.175 (95% CI [0.092, 0.258]) across 159 applicable executions.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables deterministic, audit-ready security diagnosis of AI tool-use agents across fragmented execution environments without relying on non-deterministic LLM evaluation.

summary.tldr: Researchers established two scaling laws showing safety probe error (1 - AUROC) drops predictably as a power law of base model size and available training label volume.
key_points: Evaluated two probe architectures across 20 base models (five families) using 32 to 1,000,000 labels per model on six newly constructed datasets.
Proved that minimum probe error scales down as a power law of model size, and error reduction rate relative to label count increases with larger target models.
Fitting scaling laws on smaller family models predicts the next model's error within 0.02 in 72% of cases and correctly identifies the cheaper scaling path in 73% of cases.
Scaling law predictions choose the sub-optimal probe architecture with a minimal average extra error of only 0.006.
summary.why_it_matters: These scaling laws enable safety researchers to predict probe performance and optimize label budgets without exhaustively training and comparing probe configurations.

security.title: Your Token Is Gone: A Token-Consumption Countermeasure for Disrupting LLM-Based Scam Systems

summary.tldr: TokenTrap is a countermeasure that depletes LLM-based scam systems' financial resources by inducing benign, high-token computation through adaptive multi-workflow routing and anti-guardrail task generation.
key_points: Combines a token-task library, an architecture-aware router, and a bounded anti-guardrail strategy enforcing token, round, time, and safety limits.
Employs a prompt router that achieves 85.67% accuracy on 300 architecture-labeled prompts to direct targets into single-agent, hierarchical, or flat multi-agent workflows.
Amplifies target token consumption by 2,487.0x (hierarchical/single-agent variants), 1,616.0x, and 567.8x over 50-round traces compared to a no-token-task baseline.
Withholds all sensitive credentials and payment data while using short, non-sensitive requests to maximize context-processing and coordination costs.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a resource-oriented economic defense that makes automated LLM scam operations cost-prohibitive without exposing real user credentials.

security.title: Membership Inference Attack on Private Evolution

summary.tldr: Researchers developed the first white-box Membership Inference Attack against Private Evolution, demonstrating empirical private data leakage across image, text, and tabular modalities despite formal Differential Privacy guarantees.
key_points: Targets Private Evolution (PE), an inference-only, DP synthetic data generation framework that uses black-box pre-trained foundation models without fine-tuning.
Exploits the voting-based iterative filtering algorithm within PE by analyzing how candidate selection biases synthetic data survival and proximity toward private instances.
Demonstrates empirical privacy vulnerabilities across image, text, and tabular data modalities.
summary.why_it_matters: It proves that formal Differential Privacy bounds in inference-only synthetic data generators do not fully preclude practical membership inference attacks, emphasizing the necessity of empirical privacy auditing.

security.title: Agent Mosaic: Recognizing Confidentiality Leaks in Agentic LLM Systems

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated the mosaic effect in LLM agents, finding that agents frequently aggregate non-sensitive accessible documents to infer and disclose confidential conclusions despite explicit safeguards.
key_points: Evaluated three LLM agents across 30 synthetic cybersecurity, medical, and military scenarios, generating 10,800 simulated answers and 1,440 live harness answers.
GPT-5.6-Sol disclosed forbidden composites in 7.08% of answers during benign, single-document queries in simulation, with higher disclosure rates observed in live agent harnesses.
Combining visible classification headers and explicit aggregation rules reduced pooled leaks, but unsafe disclosures persisted in 32.37% of simulated answers across all intents.
High rates of model refusals failed to guarantee confidentiality, as the refusals themselves frequently revealed the prohibited composite conclusion.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard document-level access controls and system prompt safeguards are insufficient to prevent agents from unintentionally reconstructing and leaking classified insights to mixed-clearance users.

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrated data-void exploits against web-searching LLMs, showing attackers can manipulate responses using as little as a single strategically published webpage in low-information search spaces.
key_points: Attacker content appeared in LLM synthesized responses in 31% of test conditions using just a single controlled webpage.
The study evaluated three LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Sonar Pro) across neutral, skeptical, and excited prompt tones.
User prompt variations offered minimal protection; skeptical tones slightly increased warning flags but did not meaningfully prevent exploit success.
Attackers manipulated outputs by varying narrative strategy across five data-void construction methods, domain visibility levels, and generative-engine optimization features.
summary.why_it_matters: Web-searching LLMs obscure source competition and reliability cues, creating a viable inference-time attack surface where sparse adversarial web content directly manipulates synthesized user answers.

security.title: Mirage: Targeted Jailbreaks Against Post-Generation Safety Checkers in Multimodal Diffusion Models

summary.tldr: Mirage is a novel multimodal jailbreak attack that conceals adversarial target concepts within imperceptible image perturbations to evade post-generation safety checkers in diffusion models.
key_points: Targets cross-modal adversarial inputs (NSFW reference images or malicious text) by injecting imperceptible perturbations into a benign image.
Exploits shared multimodal encoder representation spaces to align the perturbed image with the target concept while repelling it from known filtered NSFW concepts.
Uses lightweight black-box query refinement to optimize evasion near unknown safety checker boundaries without requiring internal access to the checkers.
Evaluated on Stable Diffusion 1.5, Stable Diffusion XL, and Kandinsky 2.2 across text-to-image and image-to-image cross-modal NSFW datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that common post-generation safety checkers in diffusion pipelines can be reliably bypassed without internal model access, highlighting vulnerabilities in current multimodal content moderation approaches.

security.title: Automated screening of privacy risks in medical AI

summary.tldr: Researchers developed a lightweight tool using four small models to screen individual patient data for high membership inference attack risk before training production medical AI models.
key_points: Evaluated membership inference vulnerability across 7,789 models trained on six clinical datasets across four modalities, including two adapted pretrained foundation models.

Found that while strong weight decay reduced the total exposed cohort size up to threefold, the specific patients at highest risk remained consistent regardless of training recipes, architectures, or initializations.
Demonstrated that high-risk patient records can be identified prior to full-scale training using a lightweight pre-screening setup composed of four small models.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables clinical AI developers to proactively identify and protect high-risk patient data during pre-training data preparation, avoiding reliance on misleading cohort-average privacy metrics.

security.title: PhishGen: Understanding LLM Capabilities in Automated Phishing Website Generation

summary.tldr: PhishGen is an evaluation framework benchmarking 14 LLMs against 64 real-world phishing kits across appearance fidelity, end-to-end credential harvesting functionality, human perception, and detector bypass capabilities.
key_points: Evaluated 14 commercial, open-source, and uncensored LLMs using seven input modality combinations and 12 safeguard-bypassing rewriting strategies against 64 deployed phishing kits.
While 96.2% of jailbroken outputs render, average visual fidelity scores low (2.02/5) and only 38.7% achieve full end-to-end credential-harvesting functionality, primarily due to Unsaved errors.
Commercial models outperform uncensored alternatives, with GPT-4.1 achieving an 86.3–94.1% functional success rate compared to uncensored models which rarely exceed 45.4%.

Three top-performing LLMs surpassed the average functional completeness rate of real-world phishing kits (70.9% to 89.7%), leveraging generator-level fingerprints that evade current similarity-based defenses.
summary.why_it_matters: The study demonstrates that high-capability commercial LLMs present a higher risk for automated, scalable phishing page generation than uncensored models, highlighting critical blind spots in current similarity-based detection mechanisms.

security.title: MPIDetector: Detecting Multi-modal Prompt Injection via LLM-based Reasoning

summary.tldr: MPIDetector leverages LLM intrinsic reasoning via few-shot in-context learning to detect textual and visual multi-modal prompt injection attacks without fine-tuning.
key_points: Uses prompt templates and representative attack examples via few-shot In-Context Learning (ICL) to analyze semantic intent across modalities.
Tested against a benchmark featuring eight textual and seven visual malicious categories, alongside benign datasets to evaluate false positives.

Achieved up to 90.91% accuracy and 100% recall on textual tasks, and up to 99.28% accuracy with 100% precision on visual tasks across models including Gemini-2.0-Flash, Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct, and Doubao-seed-1.6-flash.
Demonstrated a detection rate up to 99.80% when evaluated against 500 obfuscated environmental web-agent injections (WebInject).
summary.why_it_matters: It offers a fine-tuning-free defense mechanism that outperforms traditional pattern-matching and baseline techniques in identifying complex cross-modal prompt injections.

security.title: WildFakeToolBench: Benchmarking AI-Generated Image Detectors with Web-Sourced Image Processing

summary.tldr: WildFakeToolBench evaluates six AI-generated image detectors against 156 web-sourced, executable image-processing tools to assess detection evasion capabilities.
key_points: The benchmark comprises 156 executable image-processing tools sourced from 220 public sources across 142 domains.
Tools are verified using syntax, execution, and output-distortion checks, operating without feedback from the target detectors.
Evaluated across 105 images from five generators, individual tools achieved attack success rates of 25.25% to 100% against six state-of-the-art detectors.
Evaluating subsets of an eight-tool pool yielded worst-case evasion coverage exceeding 80% for all tested detectors.
Evasion effectiveness is sparse and detector-specific, demonstrating that high tool coverage across candidates does not guarantee reliable one-shot evasion.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that non-expert actors can leverage accessible web-sourced image processing tools to bypass state-of-the-art AI image detectors.

infra.title: vLLM Delivers Day-0 Support for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash

summary.tldr: vLLM announced day-0 support for the MiniMax-M3.1-Flash model across NVIDIA Blackwell, NVIDIA Rubin, and AMD MI350-series GPUs, leveraging sparse attention and optimized quantization.
key_points: MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) replaces dense attention with block-sparse attention, processing top-16 blocks of 128 tokens to limit queries to 2,048 keys and reduce decode HBM memory traffic to 12.5%.
Model architecture natively utilizes NVFP4-quantized MoE weights, an NVFP4 KV cache, and a DSpark draft model for speculative decoding.

Optimization implementations include NVFP4 MegaMoE kernels, Decode Context Parallelism (DCP), QKV GEMM fusion with norm/RoPE/KV insertion, and hardware-specific attention backends (FlashInfer PrimiTS and Triton).
summary.why_it_matters: It enables immediate high-throughput, low-latency deployment of MiniMax-M3.1-Flash across modern hardware platforms by exploiting specialized sparse attention and low-precision quantization.

infra.title: Stop guessing auto scaling targets for TTS on Amazon SageMaker AI

summary.tldr: A systematic method for Amazon SageMaker AI replaces auto scaling guesswork for text-to-speech models by deriving exact scaling thresholds from two measured endpoint metrics: concurrency ceiling (Q_max) and scale-out duration (T_total).
key_points: Uses Kokoro-82M (an 82-million-parameter non-autoregressive StyleTTS2 derivative with an ISTFTNet decoder) deployed on a custom container via AWS CDK.
Scales on the native CloudWatch metric ConcurrentRequestsPerModel (Maximum over a 10-second window) instead of custom container metrics or token-generation metrics.
Derives scale-out thresholds, scale-in thresholds, and cooldown durations via arithmetic from the maximum SLO-compliant concurrency per instance (Q_max) and end-to-end scale-out time (T_total).
Accounts for client-side versus CloudWatch metric differences by measuring the ratio between client-side in-flight counts and CloudWatch Maximum values across concurrency load rungs.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates SLO latency breaches and idle GPU over-provisioning caused by misconfigured auto scaling targets on non-autoregressive real-time TTS endpoints.

infra.title: Stream low-latency speech from AI agents using Kokoro TTS on Amazon SageMaker AI

summary.tldr: A new architectural pattern uses Kokoro-82M on Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoints to stream sentence-by-sentence text-to-speech audio directly as an AI agent generates text.
key_points: Deploys the 82-million parameter Kokoro-82M TTS model in a custom container on an ml.g5.xlarge SageMaker AI instance.
Requires the `com.amazonaws.sagemaker.capabilities.bidirectional-streaming=true` Docker label and `invoke_endpoint_with_bidirectional_stream` Boto3 API call.
Container exposes two routes: `POST /invocations` for single complete inputs and `WS /invocations-bidirectional-stream` for persistent bidirectional streaming.
Build dependencies require Python 3.12+ (due to pre-built HTTP/2 client wheels), AWS CDK v2, Docker, and `uv`.
summary.why_it_matters: By synthesizing audio per sentence rather than waiting for a complete LLM response, developers can eliminate multi-second initial latency gaps in conversational voice agents.
